vendors.name: Oracle Primavera P6
vendors.tagline: Oracle's project scheduling and portfolio management software
vendors.market_position: Oracle Primavera P6 Enterprise Project Portfolio Management (P6 EPPM) is Oracle's software for planning, scheduling and managing projects, programs and portfolios. Oracle's documentation says it runs on-premises or in the cloud, and version 26 is the newest release in its library. It is built for large, schedule-driven projects, not for small-firm admin or accounting. Oracle also sells a separate cloud product, Oracle Primavera Cloud.
pros: Plans and schedules projects, programs and portfolios
On-premises or cloud deployment
Actively updated (version 26 in Oracle's library)
Handles portfolios, not only single projects
cons: No public price found this run; quote from Oracle or a partner
Scheduling and project control only, not accounting or ERP
More than a small contractor needs for simple jobs
Takes trained planners to run well
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based through Oracle or a partner; no price could be confirmed on Oracle's pages this run.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Mainly worth it when a Bahrain client or main contractor asks for schedules in P6 format. It does not handle invoicing, VAT or bookkeeping, so pair it with an accounting tool.

vendors.name: Oracle Aconex
vendors.tagline: Oracle's cloud document control and project collaboration platform
vendors.market_position: Oracle Aconex is a cloud platform for sharing and controlling project documents, project mail and approval workflows between the many companies on a construction project. Oracle's help centre also lists Field, Cost, Models, Packages, Tenders/Bids and Supplier Documents modules and a mobile app. Oracle agreed to buy Aconex in December 2017.
pros: Documents, project mail and approval workflows in one system
Built for many companies working on one project
Extra modules for field, cost, models and tenders
Mobile app for site teams
cons: No public price found this run; quote from Oracle
Document control, not accounting or ERP
Heavy for small jobs with few parties
Help centre not offered in Arabic
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based through Oracle; no price could be confirmed on Oracle's pages this run.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Aconex controls project documents and correspondence; it does not issue invoices or handle VAT, so pair it with an accounting tool.

vendors.name: Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud)
vendors.tagline: Autodesk's construction platform, now sold under the Autodesk Forma name
vendors.market_position: Autodesk Construction Cloud became part of Autodesk Forma on 24 March 2026, and its products were renamed: Autodesk Build is now Forma Build, alongside Forma Data Management, Forma Takeoff, Forma Estimate and Model Management tools such as Navisworks. Autodesk sells them in bundles for model management, preconstruction and construction operations. It suits firms whose projects already use Autodesk models.
pros: Covers document control, takeoff, estimating and field work
Model tools such as Navisworks in the same family
Bundles priced by user, project or account
Free trials offered on Autodesk's site
cons: No public prices; bundles are quote-based
Product names changed in March 2026, so older guides are out of date
No confirmed Bahrain reseller found this run
Overlaps a project tool you may already own
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; Autodesk's pricing page lists Model Management, Preconstruction and Construction Operations bundles with 'Get a Quote' and no public prices.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Worth considering if your Bahrain projects already use Autodesk models, for example in Navisworks. Ask Autodesk for a local partner before buying, as no Bahrain reseller could be confirmed.

vendors.name: Bentley Systems
vendors.tagline: Infrastructure engineering software (STAAD.Pro, OpenRoads, MicroStation)
vendors.market_position: Bentley Systems makes engineering software for infrastructure: STAAD.Pro for structural analysis and design, OpenRoads Designer for road design, MicroStation for CAD, PLAXIS for geotechnical analysis and ProjectWise for project delivery. It is design and analysis software for engineers, not site management or accounting. Bentley lists regional offices in Dubai and Al Khobar, Saudi Arabia, but none in Bahrain.
pros: Structural, road, geotechnical and pipe design tools
Published prices for many products
Free trial offered for STAAD.Pro
Regional offices in Dubai and Al Khobar
cons: Engineering design software, not site or office admin
Annual per-user subscriptions paid upfront
No Bahrain office or confirmed local reseller
Specialist tools with a learning curve for each discipline
vendors.typical_pricing: Published in USD on bentley.com: STAAD.Pro from $3,995, STAAD.Pro Advanced from $5,490 and Structural WorkSuite from $6,097, each a 12-month Virtuoso subscription for one named user paid upfront. The site also shows MicroStation from $2,656 and ProjectWise from $312. Enterprise licensing is quote-based.
vendors.ba_specific_note: For structural, road and utility design work rather than general contracting or accounting. Bentley lists no Bahrain office; its nearest listed offices are in Al Khobar, Saudi Arabia, and Dubai.

vendors.name: Procore
vendors.tagline: Construction management platform priced on construction volume, with unlimited users
vendors.market_position: Procore is a US-listed construction management platform covering project management, quality and safety, and financials. It charges an upfront annual fee per product based on a company's annual construction volume, with unlimited users included. Procore runs a UAE English site with a Dubai phone number; no Bahrain office or local partner was confirmed.
pros: Unlimited users on every contract
Unlimited data storage included
Project, quality, safety and financial tools in one platform
UAE English site and Dubai phone line for Gulf buyers
cons: No public prices; quote based on construction volume
Upfront annual fee per product
No confirmed Bahrain office or local partner
Not an accounting system; pair with your books
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; Procore charges an upfront annual fee per product based on annual construction volume, with unlimited users and unlimited storage, and publishes no amounts.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Procore's nearest listed contact is its UAE site and Dubai phone number; ask who will implement and support it before committing on a Bahrain project.

vendors.name: PlanRadar
vendors.tagline: Site documentation, defect and snagging app with published prices
vendors.market_position: PlanRadar, made by PlanRadar GmbH of Vienna, is an app for site documentation, defects, snagging and inspections on plans and BIM models. It publishes per-user prices and a 30-day free trial, and runs UAE English and Arabic sites. PlanRadar says it has over 200,000 users across 75+ countries; no Gulf office address is listed.
pros: Published per-user prices and a 30-day free trial
Unlimited subcontractors and watchers on every plan
Arabic-language UAE site
Defects and snagging tracked on digital plans
cons: No Gulf office address listed
Field and QA focus, not accounting or ERP
Per-user cost grows with the team
Starter and Pro plans capped at 10 users
vendors.typical_pricing: Published in USD: Basic $32 a month (one user), Starter $107 and Pro $159 per user per month (each up to 10 users); annual billing saves more than 10%, according to PlanRadar. Enterprise is quote-based. 30-day free trial.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Easy to trial on one Bahrain project: the 30-day free trial needs no credit card, and subcontractors join free. Support comes from outside Bahrain, as no Gulf office is listed.

vendors.name: Focus Softnet
vendors.tagline: Gulf ERP vendor with a Manama office and a real estate and construction edition
vendors.market_position: Focus Softnet sells ERP software, led by its Focus X cloud ERP, plus a real estate and construction edition with project management, cost control and property management. It has a Bahrain company, Focus Softnet Bahrain Computer Consultants WLL, with an office in Manama, and offices in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar and Oman. Focus Softnet says it has been in business for 30+ years across 17+ countries.
pros: Registered Bahrain company with a Manama office
Project cost control and property management in one ERP
Offices across the other GCC countries
Wide product range (ERP, CRM, HCM, warehouse)
cons: No public prices; demo and quote only
Construction page lists no BOQ or progress-billing features
Broad ERP: expect an implementation project
Bahrain pages make no specific Bahrain VAT claims
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; Focus Softnet publishes no prices and offers a demo request instead.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Focus Softnet has a Bahrain company and a Manama office (Building 1311, Road 525), so there is a local office to ask about implementation and support. Ask for a demo of the construction features you need, as the website lists only project management and cost control.

vendors.name: PACT ERP
vendors.tagline: ERP with a construction and contracting edition and a Manama partner
vendors.market_position: PACT ERP, from PACT Software Services, is a business ERP covering finance, inventory, procurement, sales, HR and payroll, with a construction and contracting edition for project scheduling, procurement and cost control. PACT has offices in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah and lists Aramis Enterprise Solutions WLL in Manama as its Bahrain partner. PACT says it has 12,000+ customers worldwide.
pros: Named Bahrain partner in Manama (Aramis Enterprise Solutions)
Project scheduling, procurement and cost control in one ERP
Payroll and HR in the same system
Offices in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah
cons: No public prices; consultation and quote only
BOQ and subcontract modules not named on its website
Implementation-heavy like any ERP
No Bahrain-specific VAT or e-invoicing claims
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; PACT publishes no prices and offers a free consultation instead.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Sold and supported in Bahrain through Aramis Enterprise Solutions WLL in Manama, according to PACT. Ask the partner to demo BOQ and subcontract handling, which the website does not detail.

vendors.name: Diamond Software (Diamond ERP)
vendors.tagline: Manama-based ERP maker with a construction edition (job costing, BOQ, progress billing)
vendors.market_position: Diamond Software is a Manama-based software company whose Diamond ERP has a construction edition with job costing by project, BOQ management, subcontractor management and progress billing. Diamond says it has served 300+ clients since 2000 and that its system handles VAT reporting for Bahrain and Saudi Arabia. It publishes no prices.
pros: Office in Manama
Job costing, BOQ and progress billing listed
Subcontractor management and budget vs actual reports
Vendor-stated VAT reporting for Bahrain and Saudi Arabia
cons: No public prices
Smaller vendor than the global platforms
No BIM tools listed on its construction page
E-invoicing readiness is the vendor's own claim
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; Diamond Software publishes no prices.
vendors.ba_specific_note: A Bahrain-based vendor with its office in Manama (Road 3001, Block 330), so there is a local office for demos and support. Diamond says its ERP is ready for Bahrain VAT and e-invoicing; ask to see the VAT return reports in a demo.

vendors.name: Zoho (Books)
vendors.tagline: Cloud accounting with a Bahrain edition, VAT reports and published prices
vendors.market_position: Zoho Books is cloud accounting from Zoho with a Bahrain edition that applies VAT to sales and purchases and produces VAT reports for filing, in English or Arabic. Zoho publishes Bahrain prices in USD, from a free plan for small businesses up to an Ultimate plan. It handles invoicing, bookkeeping and project time billing, not construction management.
pros: Bahrain edition with VAT reports for filing
Published Bahrain prices and a free plan
English and Arabic interface
Projects with time and expense billing
cons: Accounting, not construction management
No construction BOQ or job-costing module listed
Extra users cost $2.5-$3 a month each
Free plan ends above 50K USD revenue a year
vendors.typical_pricing: Published in USD on Zoho's Bahrain site, per organisation per month, billed annually: Free $0 (revenue under 50K USD a year), Standard $15 (3 users), Professional $25 (5 users), Premium $35 (10 users), Elite $85 (10 users), Ultimate $200 (15 users). Billed monthly: $18, $30, $42, $99 and $249. Extra users $2.5 a month billed annually ($3 monthly). Prices exclude local taxes; 14-day free trial.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Zoho runs a Bahrain edition with VAT reports and Arabic, and its Bahrain prices are lower than its US prices. Run it alongside a site or project tool rather than expecting it to manage jobs.

vendors.name: TallyPrime
vendors.tagline: Accounting and inventory software with a Middle East edition
vendors.market_position: TallyPrime from Tally Solutions is accounting, inventory and invoicing software, sold as Silver for a single user and Gold for multiple users on monthly, yearly or lifetime licences. Its Middle East site covers UAE and Saudi VAT and e-invoicing, but has no Bahrain VAT page. Tally says 2.7M+ businesses use its software.
pros: Lifetime licence option as well as monthly and yearly plans
Accounting, inventory and invoicing in one package
Arabic-language Middle East site
Partner locator includes Bahrain
cons: No Bahrain VAT page on Tally's site
Gulf prices not readable this run; ask a partner
Accounting and inventory, not construction management
Plans auto-renew until cancelled
vendors.typical_pricing: Tally publishes prices for TallyPrime Silver (single user) and Gold (multi-user) on 1-month, 3-month, 12-month and lifetime plans, with AED, USD and SAR options; the Gulf-currency amounts could not be read this run and no Bahrain (BHD) price is shown.
vendors.ba_specific_note: If your accountant already uses Tally, it can stay the books system, but Tally's own site does not describe Bahrain VAT support; ask a Tally partner to show a Bahrain VAT return before buying.

vendors.name: Wafeq
vendors.tagline: Arabic and English cloud accounting with published Bahraini dinar prices
vendors.market_position: Wafeq is cloud accounting software with a Bahrain site in English and Arabic and prices in Bahraini dinars. It covers invoices, quotes, purchase orders, inventory, payroll and 40+ financial reports. Wafeq says more than 18,000 companies use it; its terms are issued by Wafeq FZ-LLC under Dubai (DIFC) courts.
pros: Published prices in Bahraini dinars
English and Arabic Bahrain site
Invoicing, inventory and payroll in one app
14-day free trial, no credit card
cons: No Bahrain VAT or NBR details on its Bahrain pages
Accounting, not construction management
Users per plan not stated on the pricing page
Contract disputes go to Dubai (DIFC) courts
vendors.typical_pricing: Published in BHD: Starter BHD 12, Plus BHD 15 and Premium BHD 25 a month billed monthly, or BHD 120, BHD 150 and BHD 252 paid yearly. Enterprise is quote-based and yearly only. Add-ons from BHD 7 a month. 14-day free trial.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Wafeq prices its Bahrain plans in dinars and offers an Arabic interface. Its Bahrain pages do not describe Bahrain VAT returns, so ask Wafeq to show a Bahrain VAT report before switching.

vendors.name: National Bureau for Revenue (NBR)
vendors.tagline: Bahrain's VAT authority: 10% standard rate since 1 January 2022
vendors.market_position: The National Bureau for Revenue (NBR) administers Bahrain's VAT, introduced on 1 January 2019. The standard rate rose from 5% to 10% on 1 January 2022. Registration is mandatory for resident businesses at BHD 37,500 of annual taxable revenue and voluntary from BHD 18,750, according to PwC's Worldwide Tax Summaries (reviewed July 2026).
pros: One national VAT authority (NBR)
Published registration thresholds: BHD 37,500 mandatory, BHD 18,750 voluntary
No e-invoicing mandate in force as of PwC's July 2026 review
cons: 10% standard rate on taxable supplies
Registration is mandatory once the BHD 37,500 threshold is reached
NBR carries out market inspections for VAT violations
An e-invoicing system is expected but has no confirmed start date
vendors.typical_pricing: No NBR fee schedule could be read (nbr.gov.bh blocked automated access). The cost to a business is collecting and filing VAT at the 10% standard rate.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Check that any accounting or invoicing tool applies Bahrain's 10% standard rate. There is no e-invoicing mandate in force yet, but PwC notes the market expects one similar to Saudi Arabia's and Gulf Daily News reported an e-invoicing push in July 2026, so choose software that can adapt.

vendors.name: CRPEP (Engineering Professions Regulator)
vendors.tagline: Licences engineers and engineering offices in Bahrain
vendors.market_position: The Council for Regulating the Practice of Engineering Professions (CRPEP) is the government body that licenses engineers and engineering offices in Bahrain under Law No. 51 of 2014, with implementing regulations issued in 2023. Benayat requires new-building permit applications to be filed through a CRPEP-licensed engineering office.
pros: Clear statutory basis: Law No. 51 of 2014
Engineer licences are processed in 3 working days online, according to the national portal
Published fee schedule on the Bahrain national portal
A CRPEP office licence lets you file new-building permits on Benayat
cons: Engineers and engineering offices need a CRPEP licence to practise
Office licences cost BD 100-4,000 to issue, plus an application fee
Offices must hold professional indemnity insurance
Office licence applications take 25 working days online
vendors.typical_pricing: Engineer licence: BD 15 application plus BD 40 issuance (category D) or BD 115 (categories A, B, C and K). Engineering office licence: BD 100-1,000 application by category, BD 15 per engineer, BD 100-4,000 issuance and BD 100-2,000 renewal per discipline (Bahrain national portal).
vendors.ba_specific_note: If you run an engineering office in Bahrain, you need a CRPEP office licence and licensed engineers; that licence is what lets you file new-building and large-addition permits on Benayat. Owners can file small additions under 50 square metres themselves.

vendors.name: Ministry of Works Contractor Prequalification
vendors.tagline: Ministry of Works contractor prequalification by category and grade
vendors.market_position: Bahrain's Ministry of Works prequalifies contractors for its building, roads, sanitary and landscape works through an online prequalification system. Main categories are graded AA to F, specialised categories A to C and electrical works 1 to 3, and international contractors may apply only for the top grade. Fees are set by Decision No. 9 of 2017 and Ministerial Decision No. 13 of 2021.
pros: Published list of categories and grades
Online application, upgrade, re-evaluation and renewal forms
Application fee of BD 50 per prequalification application
Separate categories for building, roads, sanitary and landscape work
cons: Each category needs its own application and fee
International contractors can apply only for the top grade
Grade criteria are spread across several PDF documents
Renewals and upgrades mean repeat applications
vendors.typical_pricing: BD 50 per prequalification application (Ministry of Works instructions to contractors). Service rates are set by Decision No. 9 of 2017 and Ministerial Decision No. 13 of 2021.
vendors.ba_specific_note: If you want Ministry of Works building, road, sewerage or landscaping contracts, apply for prequalification in each category you work in through the Ministry's online system. Tender notices themselves are published on the Tender Board's portal.

vendors.name: Bahrain Tender Board
vendors.tagline: Bahrain's regulator of government tenders and its eTendering system
vendors.market_position: Established in 2002 by Legislative Decree No. 36, the Tender Board describes itself as an independent regulator of government procurement in Bahrain. Its FAQ says it oversees purchases above BHD 50,000 by government purchasing authorities and above BHD 100,000 by fully government-owned companies. The Board reports 1,930 tenders awarded in 2025.
pros: One eTendering system for tenders under its oversight
Published laws, FAQs and tender notices
Formal route to request reconsideration of tender procedures
International suppliers can register with their home registration
cons: Bidders must register on the eTendering system and be approved
A CR that is active without a licence cannot be approved
Each branch CR needs a separate registration
Tender documents must be purchased before you can bid
vendors.typical_pricing: No supplier registration fee is stated on the Tender Board site. Suppliers must buy the tender document for each tender before uploading a bid; the FAQ does not list document prices.
vendors.ba_specific_note: To bid for larger government contracts, register your company on the Tender Board's eTendering system with an active, licensed CR. The Ministry of Works also runs its own contractor prequalification by category, so check both if you target its projects.

vendors.name: LMRA & Bahrainisation
vendors.tagline: Bahrain's work-permit authority for expatriate staff
vendors.market_position: The Labour Market Regulatory Authority (LMRA) issues and renews work permits for expatriate employees in Bahrain under Resolution No. 76 of 2008, with employer fees set by Resolution No. 26 of 2008. Employers below their required Bahrainisation ratio can still obtain permits through the Parallel Bahrainisation System by paying a higher fee.
pros: One authority for expatriate work permits
Remote work permit renewal, processed in 1 working day according to the national portal
Fees published on the Bahrain national portal
Parallel Bahrainisation lets firms below their ratio still hire
cons: Work permit fee of BHD 195 a year per employee, plus an admin fee
Extra fee for permits outside the Bahrainisation ratio
Bahrainisation ratios limit how many expatriates you can hire at the normal fee
Permits run for six months to two years, then need renewal
vendors.typical_pricing: Work permit (commercial sector) renewal: BHD 97.5 for 6 months, BHD 195 for one year or BHD 390 for two years, plus a BHD 5 admin fee (Bahrain national portal). Permits outside the Bahrainisation ratio cost more; one portal service lists BHD 250 a year.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Budget LMRA work permit fees (BHD 195 per expatriate per year at the standard rate) into your labour costs, and check your Bahrainisation ratio: permits above it are available through the Parallel Bahrainisation System at a higher fee.

vendors.name: Benayat (Building Permits)
vendors.tagline: Bahrain's official online building-permit system
vendors.market_position: Benayat is the Kingdom of Bahrain's official system for issuing building permits for all types of building projects. New buildings and large additions are filed through an engineering office licensed by CRPEP, while owners can file small additions and demolitions themselves. Government entities including the General Directorate of Civil Defense give their input through the system, and Gulf Daily News reported 6,550 permits issued in 2024.
pros: One online portal for applications, status and fee payment
Government inputs within 5 working days, according to the Benayat FAQ
Fees and deposit rules published in the FAQ
Owners can file small additions and demolitions directly
cons: A permit is needed before construction starts
New buildings and large additions must go through a CRPEP-licensed office
Refundable insurance deposit of up to BD 20,000 on top of the fee
Permits are valid for one year from issue
vendors.typical_pricing: Permit fee 250 fils per square metre (residential) or 500 fils (non-residential); telecom towers BD 500. Plus a refundable insurance deposit of 500 fils per square metre (residential) or BD 1 (non-residential), capped at BD 20,000 (Benayat FAQ).
vendors.ba_specific_note: Build the Benayat permit into every Bahrain project programme: appoint a CRPEP-licensed engineering office, allow for pre-approvals (up to 10 working days) and the Civil Defense input, and budget the refundable insurance deposit alongside the permit fee.

vendors.name: Civil Defence (Fire Safety)
vendors.tagline: Fire-safety approvals from the General Directorate of Civil Defense
vendors.market_position: The General Directorate of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) gives input on building permits in Benayat, and its approval letter is required for a building's completion certificate. It also reviews fire-protection designs for commercial centres, tall buildings and buildings over 1,000 square metres, and licenses contractors that install and maintain fire alarms and suppression systems.
pros: Civil Defense input is built into the Benayat permit process
Certificates can be requested and verified online through bahrain.bh
Fees published on the Bahrain national portal
Design review for large buildings is processed in 14 working days
cons: Completion certificates need a Civil Defense approval letter
Design review fee of BD 300 for large and tall buildings
Fire-system installers need their own Civil Defense licence
Installer licences require licensed engineers and technicians on staff
vendors.typical_pricing: Design review for commercial centres, tall buildings and buildings over 1,000 square metres: BD 300. Licence to install and maintain alarms and fire suppression devices: BD 100 per product. Fees set by Ministerial Resolution No. 100 of 2016 (Bahrain national portal).
vendors.ba_specific_note: Plan for Civil Defense early: it gives input on the Benayat permit, larger buildings need a fire-protection design review, and you cannot get the completion certificate without its approval letter. If you install fire alarms or suppression systems, you need a Civil Defense installer licence.

vendors.name: Bahrain Kuwait Insurance Company (BKIC)
vendors.tagline: Bahrain Kuwait Insurance Company, trading as GIG Bahrain
vendors.market_position: Bahrain Kuwait Insurance Company (BKIC) trades as GIG Bahrain and is part of the Gulf Insurance Group (GIG); its Takaful arm, Takaful International, describes itself as a subsidiary of GIG Bahrain. AM Best affirmed the ratings of BKIC and its subsidiary in September 2026, reported as A- (Excellent). Its website has Bahrain and Kuwait sections.
pros: Part of the regional Gulf Insurance Group
AM Best ratings affirmed in September 2026
Operates in both Bahrain and Kuwait
Group Takaful arm offers Contractors All Risks cover
cons: No engineering or contractor product page found on its website
Quote-only: no public prices for commercial cover
Same group as Takaful International, so not an independent second quote
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices for commercial or contractor cover.
vendors.ba_specific_note: BKIC and GIG Bahrain are the same company, and Takaful International is its subsidiary. Ask BKIC or a broker directly whether it writes Contractors All Risks or professional indemnity for your project, since its website does not list engineering cover.

vendors.name: Solidarity Bahrain
vendors.tagline: Bahrain insurer that took over Bahrain National Insurance (bni) in 2025
vendors.market_position: Solidarity Bahrain sells motor, health, life, travel and business insurance. Its group completed the acquisition of Bahrain National Insurance (bni) and Bahrain National Life (bnl) in April 2025, and Solidarity Bahrain acquired bni from its parent in October 2025 after Central Bank of Bahrain approval. Gulf Daily News reported a merger of bni and bnl in February 2026.
pros: Business insurance section alongside personal lines
Enlarged by the 2025 bni acquisition
Central Bank of Bahrain approved the bni deal
Also sells cyber cover
cons: No engineering or Contractors All Risks page found on its website
Quote-only: no public prices for business cover
AM Best kept its ratings under review with negative implications in July 2026
bni integration is recent, so check which entity issues your policy
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices for business cover.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Solidarity Bahrain acquired Bahrain National Insurance (bni) in 2025, so treat bni and Solidarity as one group when collecting quotes. Ask directly whether it writes Contractors All Risks for your project, as its website does not list engineering cover.

vendors.name: Takaful International Company (GIG Bahrain Takaful)
vendors.tagline: Takaful (Shari'a-compliant) insurer with Contractors All Risks and other engineering cover
vendors.market_position: Takaful International Company (GIG Bahrain Takaful), established in 1989, says it was the first Islamic insurance company in Bahrain. It is a subsidiary of GIG Bahrain (Bahrain Kuwait Insurance Company) and part of the GIG group, and says it is rated A- (Excellent) by AM Best. Its engineering line covers Contractors All Risks, Erection All Risks, Machinery Breakdown and Computer All Risks.
pros: Contractors All Risks cover, extendable to third-party liability
Erection All Risks and Machinery Breakdown cover for plant
Shari'a-compliant Takaful model
Also offers business property, marine, liability and motor fleet cover
cons: Quote-only: no public prices for engineering cover
Same group as BKIC, so not an independent second quote
Product pages give short descriptions only, without policy wordings
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices for engineering or business cover.
vendors.ba_specific_note: Takaful International is the Takaful subsidiary of BKIC (GIG Bahrain), so a quote from both is two quotes from one group. It lists Contractors All Risks and Erection All Risks cover for contractors who want a Shari'a-compliant policy.

vendors.name: ProTenders
vendors.tagline: GCC construction intelligence and eTendering, with a free company-profile tier
vendors.market_position: ProTenders, operated by NuServ Ltd and launched in 2011 according to its about page, sells construction project intelligence and an eTendering tool to developers, consultants, contractors and suppliers in the six GCC states, including Bahrain. It says it tracks $82 billion of upcoming and ongoing construction projects in Bahrain, from design through tender and construction. A free company profile lets firms list their projects and bid on private tenders.
pros: Free company profile that can bid on private tenders
Tracks Bahrain projects by stage, from design to construction
Paid plan includes project participant details and alerts
eTendering tool for running your own tenders
cons: Project data needs a login; intelligence and eTendering are custom-priced
No published prices for the paid plans
No Bahrain office; listed offices are Montreal and Abu Dhabi
vendors.typical_pricing: Company Profiles: free. Construction Intelligence and Construction eTendering: custom pricing after a demo request; no published prices.
vendors.ba_specific_note: ProTenders covers Bahrain construction projects alongside the rest of the GCC. A free profile gets your firm listed and able to bid on private tenders; project leads and participant details sit in the custom-priced Construction Intelligence plan.
